thread:
sara: Hey @support — BrightHire reporting intermittent auth failures on SSE streaming. They see a 200 then a 401 after ~30s. Example request id: rq_4f7a2bdc. Need a minimal curl repro + exact headers + what traces to collect. Token rotation on their sidecar is possible.

alex: Thanks Sara. Two quick asks: (1) capture full response headers including SSE chunk boundaries, (2) capture the exact Authorization header that was used right before the failure (mask token). Also ask them to confirm system clock (NTP) — signed tokens can fail on skew.

manu: Quick reproduce check — ask them to run this to stream and capture both headers and body (no buffering):
```bash
curl -v \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: rq_4f7a2bdc" \
  --no-buffer \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=x1" > stream.log
```

kevin: Add these flags to ensure you get raw headers and chunk boundaries: `-i --raw -D headers.txt` and also `--max-time` to prevent hangs. Example: 
```bash
curl -v -i --raw -D headers.txt \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: rq_4f7a2bdc" \
  --no-buffer "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=x1" > stream.log
```

sara: Customer ran it and pasted the important bits: first chunk delivered, then at 00:12:17 UTC we see `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="expired"`. Request id `rq_4f7a2bdc` and trace header `X-Trace-Id: tr_9a12ef` present. They confirmed token rotation is ~15s.

alex: That points to the sidecar rotating tokens mid-connection. Streaming SSE expects the same auth for handshake and the lifetime of the connection. Repro strategy: 1) reproduce by swapping token at 15s, 2) verify if increasing token TTL prevents 401, 3) capture tcp pcap if possible.

manu: To collect a full debug bundle from their side: capture the curl outputs plus tcpdump and SDK debug logs. Example commands we ask them to run (one at a time):
```bash
# 1) curl capture (headers + body)
curl -v -i --raw -D headers.txt -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" --no-buffer "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=x1" > stream.log

# 2) capture encrypted packets for correlation (if allowed):
sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w capture.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443

# 3) enable client sdk debug (if using our client):
CLIENT_DEBUG=1 node reproduce.js  # or export CLIENT_DEBUG=1 and run their app
```

kevin: Also request from them: gateway and worker logs for the timestamp window (00:11:30 - 00:13:00 UTC), mask tokens in shared files, and include these headers in the bundle: `Authorization`, `X-Request-Id`, `X-Trace-Id`, `Date`. Ask them to run `date -u` and paste output.

BrightHire-SRE: Thanks — running now. Will attach `stream.log`, `headers.txt`, and `capture.pcap`. Note: our sidecar rotates tokens every 15s; we can temporarily increase to 240s for a test. ETA ~20m.

sara: Great — once they upload, please tag `@alex` and `@manu`. Also include the raw `headers.txt` (do NOT redact `X-Request-Id` or `X-Trace-Id`). :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: reminder: attach files via the support upload flow so we can fetch them into the case docket.

kevin: After bundle arrives, we'll correlate `rq_4f7a2bdc` with the ingress logs and the worker trace `tr_9a12ef`. If we see the auth header changing server-side or an auth failure from upstream OAuth, we'll escalate to infra.

sara: ACK — monitoring channel until we have the bundle. Thanks all.
